title: Adding instruction cache effect to schedulability analysis of preemptive real-time systems

extraction.paper_name: Adding Instruction Cache Effect to Schedulability Analysis of Preemptive Real-Time Systems
extraction.paper_description: This paper extends Response Time Analysis (RTA) to incorporate extrinsic instruction cache interference (cache refill penalties) caused by preemptions in fixed-priority preemptive systems.

formal_description.statement: A task tau_i is defined by the tuple (C_i, T_i, D_i, B_i)

variables.C_i: Worst-case execution time (WCET) assuming no preemptions but including intrinsic cache effects
variables.T_i: Minimum inter-arrival time or period of the task
variables.B_i: Maximum blocking time from lower priority tasks using Ceiling Semaphore Protocol (CSP)

assumptions: Ceiling Semaphore Protocol (CSP) is used to bound blocking and prevent mid-execution blocking
formal_description.conclusion: Basic task model for schedulability analysis

informal_sketch.intuition: Standard real-time task parameters modified to ensure that WCET accounts for the cache speed-up when the task runs without interruption.
steps: Identify the execution time C_i using WCET tools that assume no preemption
Determine the arrival pattern T_i and deadline D_i
Calculate B_i based on shared resource access under CSP
informal_sketch.pseudocode:
class Task:
    def __init__(self, C_i, T_i, D_i, B_i, priority):
        self.C_i = C_i
        self.T_i = T_i
        self.D_i = D_i
        self.B_i = B_i
        self.priority = priority
key_insights: C_i must include intrinsic cache behavior (cold start, hits, misses within the task itself).

formal_description.statement: The cache refill penalty gamma_j is the time required to reload cache lines displaced by a preempting task tau_j

variables.gamma_j: Cache refill penalty associated with task tau_j

assumptions: The penalty can be the time to refill the entire cache or just the lines used by the preempting task
formal_description.conclusion: Defines the overhead cost added to each preemption instance

informal_sketch.intuition: When a high-priority task runs, it evicts the instructions of the lower-priority task from the cache. When the lower-priority task resumes, it must spend extra time fetching those instructions back from main memory.
steps: Determine the number of cache lines task tau_j uses
Multiply the number of lines by the memory miss penalty
informal_sketch.pseudocode:
def calculate_refill_penalty(task_j, cache_config, memory_latency):
    # Approach 1: Full cache refill
    # penalty = cache_config.total_lines * memory_latency
    # Approach 2: Lines used by preempting task
    penalty = task_j.lines_touched * memory_latency
    return penalty
key_insights: The penalty is associated with the preempting task in this model to simplify the accounting of indirect interference.

formal_description.statement: The maximum number of preemptions suffered by task tau_i in a time window w is bounded by the sum of releases of all higher priority tasks: sum_{j in hp_i} ceil(w / T_j)

variables.w: The duration of the time window
variables.hp_i: The set of tasks with priority higher than tau_i
variables.T_j: The period of higher priority task tau_j

assumptions: Critical instant occurs when all tasks are released simultaneously
formal_description.conclusion: Provides an upper bound on the number of times the cache refill penalty can be incurred

informal_sketch.intuition: In the worst case, every time a higher-priority task is released, it preempts the current task (or a task that preempted it), eventually forcing a cache refill.
steps: For each task tau_j with higher priority than tau_i:
Calculate how many times tau_j can arrive in window w using the ceiling function
Sum these arrivals to get the total preemption count
key_insights: Even if a task doesn't directly preempt tau_i, its execution increases the response time, potentially allowing more preemptions from other tasks (indirect interference).

formal_description.statement: The direct cache interference I_i suffered by task tau_i is given by: I_i = sum_{j in hp_i} (ceil(R_i / T_j) * gamma_j) - sum_{j in hp_i} (ceil(R_i / T_j) * I_j)

variables.I_i: Direct cache interference for task tau_i
variables.I_j: Direct cache interference for task tau_j

assumptions: Tasks are ordered by priority (1 is highest)
formal_description.conclusion: Characterizes the cache penalty specifically paid by task tau_i, excluding penalties already accounted for in higher priority tasks

informal_sketch.intuition: To find the cache penalty tau_i pays, we take the total potential penalties from higher priority tasks and subtract the penalties those tasks already 'paid' for themselves when they were preempted by even higher priority tasks.
steps: Start with the highest priority task (I_1 = 0)
For task tau_i, calculate the total refill cost from all tau_j in hp_i
Subtract the scaled interference I_j of those higher priority tasks to avoid double counting
This value I_i represents the 'new' penalty introduced at priority level i
informal_sketch.pseudocode:
def calculate_direct_interference(task_i, hp_tasks, R_i, gamma_values, previous_I):
    term1 = 0
    term2 = 0
    for j in range(len(hp_tasks)):
        num_releases = math.ceil(R_i / hp_tasks[j].T_j)
        term1 += num_releases * gamma_values[j]
        term2 += num_releases * previous_I[j]
    return term1 - term2
key_insights: This recursive definition is used to prove that the simplified RTA formula correctly accounts for all cache effects without over-counting.

formal_description.statement: A task tau_i is schedulable if there exists a minimum R_i <= D_i satisfying the recurrence: w_i_n_plus_1 = C_i + B_i + sum_{j in hp_i} ceil(w_i_n / T_j) * (C_j + gamma_j)

variables.w_i_n: The response time window at iteration n
variables.C_j: WCET of higher priority task tau_j
variables.gamma_j: Cache refill penalty of task tau_j

assumptions: Instruction cache effects are modeled as an inflation of higher-priority task execution times
formal_description.conclusion: Provides the exact worst-case response time (R_i) for a task in a cached preemptive system

informal_sketch.intuition: The standard RTA formula is modified so that every time a higher-priority task tau_j executes, it is treated as if its execution time is (C_j + gamma_j). This accounts for both the task's work and the cache damage it causes to the preempted task.
steps: Calculate new_w = C_i + B_i + sum over j in hp_i of (ceil(w_i / T_j) * (C_j + gamma_j))
If new_w == w_i, then R_i = w_i; break
If new_w > D_i, then task is not schedulable; break
key_insights: By adding gamma_j to C_j, the analysis covers both direct and indirect cache interference.
The formula is monotonically increasing, ensuring convergence or deadline violation.
